rows.jp: 耳元で怒鳴られて、我に返る。
rows.en: She shouted in my ear, snapping me back to myself.

ghs.en: Yelled at right in the ears, I come to my senses.
ghs.assessment: 耳元 means right by one ear or at the narrator's ear. 'Right in the ears' uses an unnatural plural and omits the acting subject.
ghs.remedy: Use 'She shouts right into my ear, bringing me back to myself.'

highlights.text: Yelled at right in the ears, I come to my senses.

rows.jp: 「は、はい？」
「ぼーっとしてた。無視してた。傷ついた」
rows.en: “You were spacing out. Ignoring me. It hurt.”

ghs.en: Touko: "All spacing out. Ignoring me. That hurts!"
ghs.assessment: The source uses three clipped but complete accusations: he was spacing out, ignoring her, and hurt her. 'All spacing out' is not grammatical, and 'That hurts' changes the completed hurt into a present general effect.
ghs.remedy: Use 'You were spacing out. Ignoring me. It hurt.'

highlights.text: Touko: "All spacing out. Ignoring me. That hurts!"

rows.jp: 「あのなぁ」
「俺にはぼーっとする権利もないのですか？」
rows.en: “Am I not even allowed to space out?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Don't I even have the privilege of spacing out now?"
ghs.assessment: 権利 is his right, not a privilege conferred by someone, and 'now' adds a temporal contrast absent from the complaint.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Don't I even have the right to space out?'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Don't I even have the privilege of spacing out now?"

rows.jp: 「……宮澄先輩のこと考えてたりとかして」
rows.en: “...You were thinking about Miyasumi or something.”

ghs.en: Touko: "...were you thinking about Miyasumi-senpai maybe."
ghs.assessment: The tentative question needs normal English interrogative punctuation and order. 'Maybe' is left after the object and the line ends with a period.
ghs.remedy: Use '...Were you thinking about Miyasumi-senpai, maybe?'

highlights.text: Touko: "...were you thinking about Miyasumi-senpai maybe."

rows.jp: 「男のこと考えてた」

ghs.en: Touko: "A guy... but no... that's so... (blushing)"
ghs.assessment: The embarrassed reaction rejects the idea: 'A man...? No... I don't want that...' 'That's so' leaves the final objection unfinished without preserving its actual predicate.
ghs.remedy: Use 'A man...? No... I don't want that...'

highlights.text: Touko: "A guy... but no... that's so... (blushing)"

rows.jp: 「なんてこった」

highlights.text: Taichi: "The hell's that!"

rows.jp: 最悪だった。

ghs.assessment: 最悪だった judges the situation or outcome the worst. 'That was really mean' instead makes it an interpersonal act of cruelty.
ghs.remedy: Use 'This was the worst.'

highlights.text: That was really mean.

rows.jp: しかもあながち外れじゃない。
rows.en: Worse, it wasn't entirely off the mark.

ghs.en: And still it's not like it's all that strange.
ghs.assessment: あながち外れじゃない says the imagined interpretation is not entirely off the mark. 'Not all that strange' judges unusualness rather than accuracy.
ghs.remedy: Use 'And it wasn't entirely wrong, either.'

highlights.text: And still it's not like it's all that strange.

rows.jp: 「夢見る娘よ、あまり夢を見るなよ」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Dreaming lady, don't be having too many dreams!"

rows.en: “...If the Three Idiots were always like that, there'd be something to dream about.”

ghs.en: Touko: "...well, since you three stooges always gave that impression, of course there's a bit of a dream."
ghs.assessment: The source gives a conditional: if the three fools were always like that, there would be at least a little room to dream. 'Since' and 'of course' turn the hypothetical into an asserted cause and result.
ghs.remedy: Use '...If you three idiots were always like that, there might be something to dream about.'

highlights.text: Touko: "...well, since you three stooges always gave that impression, of course there's a bit of a dream."

ghs.assessment: あの二人を相手に means imagining a pure-love story involving both of those two as the relevant counterparts. 'One of those two' arbitrarily selects only one.
ghs.remedy: Use 'A pure-love story with those two...'

highlights.text: A Pure Love Story with one of those two, really!

ghs.assessment: The speaker denies that the thought is creepy and says the three fools at least look the part outwardly. 'That's not disgusting' uses a different quality, while 'as far as outwards ... can be looked at' is not grammatical English.

rows.jp: 「……俺を含めるな」

深刻な問題だぞ。
自虐ネタにしてどうにか保ってるんだ。

ghs.en: My self-deprecating routine is there to cover for it somehow.
ghs.assessment: The narrator says he barely holds himself together by turning the issue into self-deprecating material. 'Cover for it' instead suggests concealing evidence or providing an excuse.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I only manage to hold myself together by turning it into a self-deprecating joke.'

highlights.text: My self-deprecating routine is there to cover for it somehow.

rows.jp: 確かに……面貌の問題ではないのかも知れないが……。

rows.en: Even knowing that, changing how I saw myself was not so easy.

ghs.en: I can understand that as much as I like, but completely changing one's way of thinking is not so simple.
ghs.assessment: The source concedes that even knowing the truth does not make reforming one's self-image easy. 'Understand that as much as I like' changes knowledge into a voluntary amount of understanding.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Even knowing that, changing how I see myself isn't easy.'

rows.jp: だって、
だってなぁ……。

セキララー！
そんなオノマトペがどこからか聞こえた。

ghs.en: That's the onomatopoeia that was audible from someplace.
ghs.assessment: The source says an onomatopoeic cry seemed to come from somewhere. 'That's the onomatopoeia that was audible' is a deictic noun clause and removes the perception's uncertainty.
ghs.remedy: Use 'An onomatopoeic cry seems to come from somewhere.'

highlights.text: That's the onomatopoeia that was audible from someplace.

rows.jp: 「どっせーい！」
スカートのはしをつかんだまま、頭上に固定する。
rows.en: I held the hem of her skirt fixed above her head.

ghs.en: I seize the hem of the skirt, and affix it to her head.
ghs.assessment: The narrator holds the skirt hem fixed above her head. 'Affix it to her head' says the fabric is attached directly onto the head and removes the elevated position.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Keeping hold of the skirt hem, I pin it above her head.'

highlights.text: I seize the hem of the skirt, and affix it to her head.

rows.jp: 今、冬子の辱められっぷりは、並じゃない！
rows.en: Touko's humiliation was now anything but ordinary!

ghs.assessment: The source exclaims that Tōko's degree of humiliation is extraordinary. 'At levels incomparable' is an ungrammatical literal degree construction.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Tōko's humiliation is off the charts!'

highlights.text: Now, the shaming of Touko is at levels incomparable!

rows.jp: しかも公道。
rows.en: On a public road, no less.

rows.jp: さあ、どうする冬子！

ghs.assessment: The direct address requires a comma before the name.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Now, what will you do, Tōko?'

highlights.text: So, what shall you do Touko!

rows.jp: どうするッッッ、真剣サムライ娘ッッッ！（予告風）
rows.en: What would you do, real-sword samurai girl?! (Preview voice.)

ghs.en: Oh Samurai Girl of the True Blade, what will you doooooooo...! (next episode preview-like)

rows.jp: 実のところ。
殴られるのを覚悟していたし、期待してもいた。
rows.en: I was prepared for her to hit me. I even wanted her to.

ghs.en: I was prepared to get beaten, anticipated it even.

rows.jp: ところがである。
ジト目で、俺を見るばかり。
rows.en: She merely stared at me through narrowed eyes.

ghs.en: I am but stared at by reproachful eyes.
ghs.assessment: The source actively says she merely looks at him with narrowed, reproachful eyes. 'I am but stared at by reproachful eyes' makes the eyes the agent and uses a stilted passive.
ghs.remedy: Use 'She only stares at me with narrowed eyes.'

highlights.text: I am but stared at by reproachful eyes.

rows.jp: 軽く朱色に染まったりなんかしちゃって。

ghs.en: Her face dyes a light vermilion, that's it.
ghs.assessment: The source lightly describes her becoming flushed. 'Her face dyes' makes the face act on itself, and 'that's it' adds a minimizing conclusion.
ghs.remedy: Use 'She even flushes a faint vermilion.'

highlights.text: Her face dyes a light vermilion, that's it.

rows.jp: 申し訳程度におさえた手に、本気でスキャンティをガードしようという意志はない。
rows.en: The hand she held there for appearances' sake showed no serious intent to guard her scanties.

ghs.en: Holding down her hand as if in apology, there is no serious volition of guarding her Scanties.
ghs.assessment: The hand is perfunctorily holding the skirt down and shows no serious intent to guard the underwear. 'Holding down her hand' reverses hand and object, while capitalized 'Scanties' is an invented product-like label.
ghs.remedy: Use 'The hand holding it down for form's sake shows no real intention of guarding her panties.'

highlights.text: Holding down her hand as if in apology, there is no serious volition of guarding her Scanties.

rows.jp: つうかモロ見えてるし。
rows.en: I mean, I could see everything.

ghs.en: But very much all of her frankness is visible.
ghs.assessment: モロ見えてる says the intimate view is fully and plainly exposed. 'All of her frankness is visible' mistakes モロ for emotional candor and removes the physical meaning.
ghs.remedy: Use 'I mean, everything is completely visible.'

highlights.text: But very much all of her frankness is visible.

rows.jp: 「なん……で……怒ら……な？」
「……だって、誰も見てないし……」
唇が震える。
「そうじゃないだろう！？」

ghs.assessment: そうじゃないだろう rejects the premise or point: 'That's not the issue!' 'That's not true' instead disputes the factual truth of her observation.
ghs.remedy: Use 'That's not the point!'

highlights.text: Taichi: "That's not true you know?!"

rows.jp: 「どうしてめくった方が怒るの？」
rows.en: “Why are you the one getting angry when you lifted it?”

ghs.en: Touko: "Why would a skirt flip make me angry now?"
ghs.assessment: The speaker asks why the person who flipped the skirt is the one getting angry. 'Why would a skirt flip make me angry' changes the human agent into the event and makes her anger the questioned effect.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Why is the person who flipped it the one getting angry?'

highlights.text: Touko: "Why would a skirt flip make me angry now?"

rows.jp: 「そこはガーンと行くところだろう？」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Shouldn't there have been a 'dun-dun-dunnn' there?"
ghs.assessment: ガーンと行く calls for a forceful retaliatory blow or explosive response. 'Dun-dun-dunnn' turns it into a dramatic musical sting.
ghs.remedy: Use 'This is where you strike back with a bang, isn't it?'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Shouldn't there have been a 'dun-dun-dunnn' there?"

ghs.assessment: 'Some your techniques' uses two incompatible determiners.

rows.jp: 「それだけ？」
こく、と少女はうなずく。

ghs.assessment: The source says the girl gives a small nod. 'Bob and the girl gives a nod' invents an unexplained name or sound and uses incorrect subject-verb agreement.
ghs.remedy: Use 'The girl gives a small nod.'

highlights.text: Bob and the girl gives a nod.

rows.jp: 嗚呼。
ニーチェは言った。
冬子は死んだ、と。

ghs.assessment: Standard Hepburn renders 冬子 as Tōko. 'Touko' uses an unmarked long-vowel spelling.

highlights.text: "Touko is dead."

rows.jp: 否。

ghs.assessment: 否 is a direct rhetorical 'No.' 'Nay' adds an archaic English register not otherwise present in the narration.
ghs.remedy: Use 'No.'

highlights.text: Nay.

rows.en: It was not the individual named Touko who had died.

ghs.assessment: Standard Hepburn renders 冬子 as Tōko. 'Touko' uses an unmarked long-vowel spelling.
ghs.remedy: Use 'It is not the individual called Tōko who died.'

highlights.text: Touko, the individual, has not died.

rows.jp: 冬子に見立てられていた、手の早い勝ち気娘という、大いなる最大公約数的価値観が喪失せしめられたのである。
rows.en: What had been lost was the grand, greatest-common-denominator value system projected onto her: the quick-tempered, assertive girl with a fast fist.

In the analysis of Touko's character, the
quarrelsome, unyielding spirit that acts as an
enormous maximum common denominator for her values
had now been forcefully removed from her.
ghs.assessment: The lost thing is a broad projected value or archetype—the quick-to-hit, strong-willed girl that had been read into Tōko. The English calls it part of an analysis and says the trait was removed from her, treating the projection as an actual possession.
ghs.remedy: Use 'What was lost was the great common-denominator ideal projected onto Tōko: the quick-to-hit, strong-willed girl.'

highlights.text:
In the analysis of Touko's character, the
quarrelsome, unyielding spirit that acts as an

ghs.remedy: Use 'Tōko had become real again.'

But me, I like the Touko that is always

ghs.assessment: 舌 is her tongue, not her lip. The English moves the intimate action to a different body part.
ghs.remedy: Use 'When I suck lightly on her tongue, she flounders as if she is drowning.'

highlights.text: suck a bit on her lip, and she flounders as if drowning, up, up, up.

rows.jp: でも反面、彼女の口腔は炉のように熱い。
rows.en: Yet her mouth was as hot as a furnace.

ghs.en: But on the other hand, the insides of her mouth have the heat of a furnace.

rows.jp: 舌もクリームめいて柔らかく、味わうと陶然とする。
rows.en: Her tongue was soft as cream, and tasting it left me intoxicated.

ghs.en: Her tongue too has the softness of cream. It's an intoxicating flavor.

rows.jp: 俺は冬子とのラブラチオな日々に思いを馳せた。%N※ラブラチオ＝太一語。口唇愛撫全般を意味する……らしい。由来不明。ラブ＋フェラチオだと思われる。
rows.en: I thought back on my days of lovelatio with Touko.%N*Lovelatio: Taichi-speak. Apparently means all forms of lip caress. Origin unknown. Probably love + fellatio.

rows.jp: と。
「スカポンターーーーーーーーーーンッッッ！！」
どかーん！

ghs.assessment: どかーん is an explosive crash or boom. 'Bokan' substitutes the title word from the preceding reference instead of rendering the impact sound.
ghs.remedy: Use 'Boom!'

highlights.text: Bokan!

rows.jp: 「これこれーーーーーーっ！！」

ghs.assessment: これこれ is the narrator's excited approving or demonstrative cry in response to the referenced bit. 'Helpy help' invents a plea for rescue and reverses the utterance's function.
ghs.remedy: Use a context-consistent cry such as 'That's it!'

highlights.text: Taichi: "Helpy heeeeeeeeelp!!!"

rows.jp: 舞いながら俺は思った。
rows.en: As I went flying, I thought—

ghs.en: As I was fluttering through the air, I thought,

rows.jp: もういない、新川豊という男のことを。
rows.en: of Yutaka Shinkawa, a man who was no longer here.

ghs.en: about Shinkawa Yutaka, the man that was no more.
ghs.assessment: The personal name 新川豊 should be presented in standard Hepburn as Yutaka Shinkawa in ordinary English name order. 'Shinkawa Yutaka' retains Japanese order without an edition-wide reason.
ghs.remedy: Use 'of Yutaka Shinkawa, the man who was no longer here.'

highlights.text: about Shinkawa Yutaka, the man that was no more.
